progressSummary: Audited V3-06 requires repair; WIP baseline preserved when a safe delta existed.

openFindings.problem: The in-memory withTransaction still snapshots/restores only contributionRepo, todoRepo and the sync buffer/cursor state. Expenses, settlements, persistent tasks, members, memberships and households are NOT snapshotted, so a mid-transaction failure leaves partial writes in those business tables. The objective explicitly requires: 'Extend the in-memory withTransaction to snapshot/restore ALL affected repos (expenses, settlements, tasks, members, memberships, households, and the sync buffer/cursor state).' Only InMemoryContributionEntryRepository and InMemoryTodoRepository implement snapshot()/restoreFromSnapshot(); the other in-memory repos have no snapshot support.
openFindings.evidence: RepositoryFactory.ts lines 360-371: 'const contribSnap = contributionRepo.snapshot(); const todoSnap = todoRepo.snapshot(); const syncCursorsSnap = baseSyncState.snapshotCursors(); const syncRecordsSnap = baseSyncState.snapshotRecords(); ... contributionRepo.restoreFromSnapshot(contribSnap); todoRepo.restoreFromSnapshot(todoSnap); baseSyncState.restoreCursors(syncCursorsSnap); baseSyncState.restoreRecords(syncRecordsSnap);'. Independent verification: a transaction that writes an expense then a contribution then throws leaves the expense in the business table ('expenses after rollback: 1 (expected 0)') while the contribution is rolled back ('contributions after rollback: 0') — a partial update survives.
openFindings.requiredFix: Add snapshot()/restoreFromSnapshot() to InMemoryExpenseEntryRepository, InMemorySettlementRepository, InMemoryPersistentTaskRepository, InMemoryMemberRepository, InMemoryMembershipRepository and InMemoryHouseholdRepository, and include all of them (plus the sync buffer/cursor state) in the in-memory withTransaction snapshot/restore so any throw rolls back every business table.
openFindings.verification: Add a failure-injection test that writes to multiple business tables (e.g. expense + contribution + settlement) inside withTransaction, throws, and asserts ALL business tables are unchanged after rollback.

openFindings.problem: The failure-injection test does not exercise the production data path and does not assert 'no business table was partially updated'. The test builds a hand-rolled replica of MaterializingSyncState inside the test (an anonymous class with its own applyDeltas implementation) instead of calling the production repos.syncState.applyDeltas, and it only asserts the contribution table (failedEntry null) plus cursor <= 1. The objective requires: 'Add a test that injects a real failing materialization (a repo error, not a silently-skipped malformed payload) and asserts the cursor did not advance AND no business table was partially updated.' The test would pass even if the production MaterializingSyncState.applyDeltas advanced the cursor outside the transaction or left partial writes in other tables.
openFindings.evidence: Test lines 88-110 construct 'new (class { inner = baseSyncState; getRepos = () => failingRepos; ... async applyDeltas(...) { ... return repos.withTransaction(async () => { await materializeDeltas(...); await baseSyncState.storeLocalRecords(...); if (pullCursorToAdvance) await baseSyncState.setCursor(...); }); } })()' — a replica, not the production applyDeltas. The assertions only check cursorAfterFail <= 1 and failedEntry null for the contribution table.
openFindings.requiredFix: Inject the failing repo into the real repository set (e.g. replace repos.contributions/repos.expenses with a throwing implementation before calling repos.syncState.applyDeltas or pullDeltas on the production MaterializingSyncState) and assert the cursor did not advance AND every business table (contributions, expenses, settlements, todos, persistent_tasks, members, memberships, households) is unchanged.
openFindings.verification: The new test fails if the production applyDeltas is reverted to non-transactional behavior or if withTransaction snapshot coverage is incomplete.

openFindings.problem: Hostile tests still only construct the scoped facade manually (createScopedRepositories(repos, 'user-stranger')) and never exercise the path the app actually uses. The objective requires: 'Hostile tests must exercise the path the app uses (e.g. through AppContext or the use-case layer), not only a manually constructed facade.' No AppProvider/useApp test exists anywhere in the suite, so nothing proves the AppContext wiring actually rejects cross-tenant access or that the app path is scoped.
openFindings.evidence: grep for AppProvider/useApp in __tests__ returns no matches; all Finding #3 tests call createScopedRepositories directly with a manually chosen callerUserId.
openFindings.requiredFix: Add hostile tests that drive the app-level data-access path: render AppProvider, sign in as a user, and assert cross-tenant reads/writes through the repos exposed by useApp() are rejected with CROSS_TENANT while legitimate member reads/writes succeed (or drive the use-case layer, e.g. completeTodoAtomic).
openFindings.verification: The hostile test fails if AppContext stops wrapping repos with the scoped facade.

openFindings.problem: The AppContext scoping wiring breaks the invitation-acceptance flow and stale-scopes across sign-in/sign-out. (a) join/[token].tsx reads repos.households.getById(invitation.householdId) and repos.memberships.getByHousehold(...) BEFORE the user is a member; with the scoped facade these throw AuthorizationError(CROSS_TENANT), so a signed-in user can never resolve or accept an invitation — a regression of the V3-06 'atomic acceptance (membership + member)' criterion. (b) signOut does not reset reposRef, so a second user signing in wraps the already-scoped repos again; the inner stale caller (previous user) blocks legitimate access.
openFindings.evidence: Independent verification: 'JOIN FLOW BREAKS: AuthorizationError CROSS_TENANT User joiner is not a member of household h-join' on repos.households.getById; 'MEMBERSHIP CREATE BLOCKED: AuthorizationError CROSS_TENANT' on memberships.create (the first-membership exception does not apply because the household already has the owner's membership); double-wrap check: 'B reads own group h-B BLOCKED (BUG): CROSS_TENANT' after A signed out and B signed in.
openFindings.requiredFix: Allow the invitation-acceptance path to read the invited household and create the invitee's membership (e.g. invitation-token-scoped read + membership creation authorized by the invitation, or a dedicated join use-case), and re-scope from the raw repos on every sign-in (reset reposRef on signOut, or keep the raw repos and wrap exactly once per sign-in) so the callerUserId is always the current user.
openFindings.verification: Add a test: sign in as a non-member, resolve an invitation, complete atomic acceptance (membership + member) through the app path; and a test: sign in as A, sign out, sign in as B, then B can read B's own group and is blocked from A's group.

openFindings.problem: The SQLite sync tests do not run the actual sync pipeline. They use raw SqliteSyncStateRepository + SqliteContributionEntryRepository: test 1 calls the raw applyDeltas (buffer-only, no materialization) and then manually seeds the business table ('Materialize into business table manually'); test 2 manually constructs the dirty record and calls storeLocalRecords instead of going through the SyncRecording wrapper. The objective requires: 'Add a test that runs the sync pipeline (applyDeltas materialization + wrapper dirty recording + pushDeltas) against the SQLite-backed repositories ... proving remote delta -> business record readable and local write -> getDirtyRecords payload' (or a shared contract test on both implementations). The factory's SQLite wiring (MaterializingSyncState + SyncRecording wrappers around raw SQLite repos) is never exercised.
openFindings.evidence: Test lines 591-593: 'await contributions.seed([{ ...entity, id: 'c-sql-remote' }])' — manual materialization; lines 616-626 manually build dirtyRecord and call syncState.storeLocalRecords — the wrapper is bypassed.
openFindings.requiredFix: Wire the SQLite repos exactly as the factory does in the test (raw SQLite repos + SyncRecording* wrappers + MaterializingSyncState, using the mocked expo-sqlite driver), or export a testable factory path, then prove: remote delta via applyDeltas -> business record readable; local write via the wrapped repo -> getDirtyRecords returns the payload; pushDeltas sends it.
openFindings.verification: The new test fails if the SQLite path drops the MaterializingSyncState/wrapper wiring.

openFindings.problem: Persistent tasks and invitations remain unscoped in the app path. The objective requires 'every getByHousehold/create/update/delete verifies membership'. repos.tasks (PersistentTaskRepository: getByHousehold/create/delete) and repos.invitations (InvitationRepository: getByHousehold/create) are household-scoped repos used by the screens (app/(tabs)/add.tsx line 186, app/(tabs)/todos.tsx line 115, app/invite.tsx line 42, app/join/[token].tsx line 53), but createScopedRepositories leaves them unscoped, so a caller can read/write another household's persistent tasks or invitations without any membership check.
openFindings.evidence: createScopedRepositories comment lines 80-84 explicitly leaves 'tasks' and 'invitations' unscoped; no ScopedPersistentTaskRepository exists; PersistentTaskRepository has getByHousehold/create/delete (index.ts lines 93-98).
openFindings.requiredFix: Add a ScopedPersistentTaskRepository (membership check on getByHousehold/create/delete) and scope invitation reads (getByHousehold requires membership; token-based getByLinkToken/getById remain invitation-authorized) or apply equivalent membership checks in the app path.
openFindings.verification: Add a hostile test: a non-member reading another household's persistent tasks through the app path is blocked with CROSS_TENANT.
